# gqlgen: twenty-eight quiet misbehaviours, diagnosed without a test suite

The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything I have been able to pin down by standing a service up from a schema, driving it from the outside and running the bundled sample projects.

Asking a running service for data is the most visible of it. Fetching a stored record by id and selecting its name and its contact address gives null for both, even though the record was stored with both values present, while the id and the numeric age alongside them are right; a record holding only a name also answers null for that name, and records stored with those two left unset still answer null as they should, so only the populated case is wrong. Estimating beforehand what a query will cost gives the wrong figure whenever a field is reached through an abstract type: instead of the largest cost among the concrete types behind it, some other number comes out, while plain nesting, fragments, inline fragments, per-field custom costs, negative custom values and the overflow guard all still add up as before.

Several things go wrong when one call is asked to answer for a whole group of parents at once. Asking for the incoming source records that lie behind such a group skips the first parent: with one parent the answer comes back empty instead of holding that parent's record, and with two the entries no longer line up with what was handed in.
